tasks.context: Following a request while preparing for a visitor.
tasks.objective: Combine 大きいコップ with the later 青いコップ request. The man's suggested red cup is explicitly rejected. In the numbered picture, the large blue cup is 3.
tasks.visualSupply: Four equally presented numbered cups in a two-by-two grid: 1, small blue; 2, large red; 3, large blue; 4, small red. The cups have the same shape apart from size. No selected item, people, tea, arrows or answer-bearing caption is shown.

tasks.context: Responding to an offer of help.
tasks.objective: 持ちましょうか offers the speaker's help. ありがとうございます。お願いします accepts that offer. A natural polite refusal could also fit in ordinary conversation, but none is included as a supposedly wrong choice here.
tasks.visualSupply: None; all question evidence is auditory and choices follow the declared text/audio presentation.

tasks.context: Choosing what the indicated person says at the current stage of an activity.
tasks.objective: The scene supplies the speaker's role: the arrow points to the photographer, who is aiming a camera at two friends. これから写真を撮ります supplies the event stage. Asking the friends to look toward the camera fits both.
tasks.visualSupply: Three adults in a park. On the left, one person holds a camera up, with its lens aimed at the other two people standing together on the right. A single arrow points to the camera holder. There is no camera handover, photograph print, speech bubble, answer number or selected response.

tasks.context: Listening for the reason for a purchase.
tasks.objective: The focus is why he needs two tickets. He will attend with his younger brother and buy both tickets himself. The woman's proposed Saturday plan does not become the final plan.
tasks.visualSupply: None; all question evidence is auditory and choices follow the declared text/audio presentation.

tasks.context: Two people are talking at a museum entrance. What will the man take out of his bag?
tasks.objective: Worked example: combine the permitted notebook with the later decisions to leave the drinks, food and camera. The notebook is the only listed item to take inside.
tasks.visualSupply: None; all question evidence is auditory and choices follow the declared text/audio presentation.

tasks.context: They are talking about a watch repair. When will the woman come to collect the watch?
tasks.objective: Worked example: distinguish possible completion from the agreed collection time. Today's work, Wednesday closure and Thursday morning appointment leave Thursday afternoon.
tasks.visualSupply: None; all question evidence is auditory and choices follow the declared text/audio presentation.

tasks.context: The purchase cost five hundred yen. The customer gave one thousand yen but received only one hundred yen in change. What does the person indicated by the arrow say?
tasks.objective: Worked example: the amounts reveal short change, but either participant could speak about that problem. First use the picture to identify the marked person as the customer. He points out the short change; the cashier would apologize and return the missing four hundred yen. Asking for a discount addresses a different problem.
tasks.visualSupply: A checkout counter separates customer A on the left from employee B on the right. A holds a small coin on an open palm. A bag rests on the counter. A single arrow points to A. No prices, speech bubbles or answer labels are printed.

tasks.context: I'm sorry, I couldn't hear clearly. Please tell me your name once more.
tasks.objective: Worked example: identify what information is requested after もう一度. Repeating the name answers it; buying a phone and the current time are unrelated.
tasks.visualSupply: None; all question evidence is auditory and choices follow the declared text/audio presentation.

tasks.context: Two people are talking while looking for a room. How much is the room the woman likes?
tasks.objective: Identify the selected second-floor room, then retain its quoted monthly rent of sixty thousand yen.
tasks.visualSupply: None; all question evidence is auditory and choices follow the declared text/audio presentation.

tasks.context: A parent and child are talking at an aquarium. Where will the child wait for his mother?
tasks.objective: The mother's final instruction and the child's confirmation agree. Earlier proposed locations do not become the meeting place.

tasks.context: They are talking about a letter to a friend. Why will the woman enclose a photograph?
tasks.objective: Listen for the purpose expressed by 分かるように. The letter sends a current appearance cue, not a new address or birthday gift.
tasks.visualSupply: None; all question evidence is auditory and choices follow the declared text/audio presentation.

tasks.context: They are talking about work at a bookshop. Why does the man work only on Sundays?
tasks.objective: His own availability, not the bookshop's opening days, controls the schedule. Combine weekday school with Saturday help at his family's shop.
tasks.visualSupply: None; all question evidence is auditory and choices follow the declared text/audio presentation.

tasks.context: It has suddenly started raining. May I borrow this umbrella until I go home?
tasks.objective: 借りてもいいですか asks permission. An appropriate refusal would also be possible, but none is offered among these distractors.
tasks.visualSupply: None; all question evidence is auditory and choices follow the declared text/audio presentation.

tasks.context: Someone has dropped a cup at work. The cup belongs to the person on the right. Look at the picture. What does the person indicated by the arrow say?
tasks.objective: The completed accident requires an apology from the person who caused it, not an instruction to the owner or thanks alone.
tasks.visualSupply: Two coworkers stand on opposite sides of an office desk. A broken cup with a few separated pieces is on the floor by person A on the left, who still holds its detached handle. A single arrow points to A. Person B stands on the right. No speech bubbles or option labels.

tasks.context: A card has fallen inside a bus. It seems to have fallen from the pocket of the person on the right. What does the person indicated by the arrow say?
tasks.objective: The audio locates the apparent owner on the right. The picture identifies the marked speaker as the other person, bending toward the card. He checks ownership rather than confirming that the card is his.
tasks.visualSupply: Inside a bus, person A bends toward a small rectangular card on the floor. Person B stands in front of A facing away, with a visible coat pocket. A single arrow points to A. The card has no readable name or answer-bearing text.

tasks.objective: The picture identifies the marked person as the current seat occupant. The audio says the standing stranger seems tired. Offering that person the seat fits; asking permission to sit reverses the roles.
